_about: Known defects of THIS hardware and build, as data rather than as prose
scattered over six documents. setup/lib/defects.py evaluates them against
the running server and the build stamp; setup/check.sh prints the result.
The field that matters most is `shows_as`. On gfx1151 the dangerous
defects do not raise — they degrade the output, and nothing in a normal
stack notices. A registry that only listed crashes would list the
harmless half.
silent        wrong output, no error anywhere. The expensive kind.
loud          crash, assert or refusal. Annoying, honest.
slow          correct but slower. A tuning matter, not a hazard.
unrepeatable  correct but not reproducible — poisons MEASUREMENTS,
which is how a wrong conclusion gets written down.
`detect.kind` is deliberately small. Four kinds, no rule engine:
cmdline      a flag on the running llama-server command line
build-flag   a cmake flag in the build's .build-stamp
build-stamp  a key in the .build-stamp
manual       only a measurement can answer; `suite` names it
`upstream_check` is the RETIREMENT condition: the probe that says a
defect is gone from upstream and its mitigation can be dropped. It reads
the SOURCE on master, not an issue's state — a closed issue is a story
about a fix, the source is the fix. `defects.py --upstream` runs them.

defects.title: The HIP backend trusts prop.integrated and corrupts the KV state
defects.symptom: From some point on every answer degenerates to '////' until the server is restarted. No error, no log line.
defects.measured: Stock build, two slots, empty prefix store: CORRUPT 6/6. Patched, one slot: clean in every cell. Cost of the patch on identical bodies: prefill -6.0 %, decode unchanged. RE-MEASURED 28.08. and REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY, after two sessions had concluded the opposite from a recipe that cannot show it. bench/suites/slot-corruption.py par-two-prefixes -- two distinct prefixes CONCURRENTLY, each with a tool block -- ten fresh starts per build, side server: stock 54ee5ee 10 of 10 CORRUPT, unpatched master 5d5cb4c 10 of 10 CORRUPT, every answer of every start, never a partial. The same builds under bench/suites/stock-vs-patched.py official-rocm-np2-orig, whose docstring calls itself the exact shape the defect was found in, are clean: 18 of 18 on 26.08. and 30 of 30 on 28.08. That recipe sends SEQUENTIAL requests with NO tools and has never been able to reproduce this defect; it produced the sentence -- it does not reproduce -- twice, two days apart. TWO ONE-VARIABLE COMPARISONS on the same upstream commit 5d5cb4c: with the patch 0 of 10, and with llama.cpp PR #27311 instead of the patch 0 of 10. So the patch fixes it, and #27311 fixes it. LOCATED to ONE COMMIT of that PR: 3181ed701, ggml-backend: ring buffer graph inputs when a backend computes on host memory. The commit before it is 10 of 10 CORRUPT and the commit with it is 0 of 10; and on the FULL PR build, which is clean, the author's own escape hatch GGML_SCHED_UMA_RING=1 brings the corruption straight back, 10 of 10, same binary and same hour. MECHANISM, in the commit message's own words: graph inputs are pinned to the CPU backend in a host buffer that an integrated device also accepts, so no split input copy is made and the device reads the memory the host thread is writing -- nothing stops the host from writing the next ubatch's inputs while the device still reads the previous one. That accounts for every ingredient: two sequences in flight, worse with larger graph inputs, indifferent to speculation and KV layout and cram, impossible on Vulkan, and removed by this patch because integrated=false means the shared buffer never exists. AND THE SAME SWITCH BRINGS THE RESTORE CORRUPTION BACK on the same binary, so slot-restore-poison is not a second mechanism: a restore is just another concurrent writer into that buffer. Full evidence: bench/reports/2026-08-28_defect1-hunt/HUNT.md. Reports: bench/reports/2026-08-28_0*_slot-corruption_*. The superseded sentence follows: It does not reproduce any more — and that is NOT a fix. `git log b10577..b10631` shows no commit touching the `integrated` path; the cause is unchanged upstream and the trigger merely moved. A defect whose cause stands and whose trigger we can no longer provoke is epistemically WORSE than a reproducible one.
defects.mitigation: setup/patches/hip-integrated-off.patch, carried as a one-commit branch gfx1151-patched. Upstream disabled the same flag for CUDA with the comment 'Temporarily disabled due to issues with corrupted output' and re-enabled it for HIP in PR #24233. And since 26.08. something WATCHES for it: setup/scripts/probe.py asks the running model one question whose answer is known, every ten minutes via llama-probe.timer, and restarts the unit when the answer is degenerate. That does not prevent the fault — it moves it from `silent` to `loud`, which is the axis this file sorts by, and it bounds how long a consumer talks to a poisoned server.

upstream_check.while_present: the graph-input ring buffer has landed in master — this is the fix. Re-measure once and the patch can go: python3 bench/suites/slot-corruption.py par-two-prefixes --binary <a build without the patch> --starts 10, and python3 bench/suites/restore-safety.py --binary <same> --spec both. Both clean means nobody has to build llama.cpp any more
upstream_check.when_gone: master does not have the ring buffer yet (llama.cpp PR #27311, commit 3181ed701, open). Keep shipping the patch
upstream_check.note: UNTIL 28.08.2026 this watched info.devices[id].integrated = prop.integrated in ggml-cuda.cu, expecting the fix to delete it. It does not. That line is at ggml-cuda.cu:306 in master AND in a build containing #27311 that measures 0 of 10 corrupt where master is 10 of 10 — so the probe could only ever say keep. Measured: bench/reports/2026-08-28_defect1-hunt/HUNT.md

defects.title: Two slots are not safe even on the patched build
defects.symptom: Same '////' degeneration, but intermittently: a configuration that is clean on one server start is corrupt on the next.
defects.measured: RE-MEASURED 28.08. on the workload that reproduces defect 1 deterministically (slot-corruption.py par-two-prefixes, ten fresh starts): the PATCHED b10631 build is 0 of 10 while the unpatched build of the same commit is 10 of 10, so on that workload the patch holds completely. This entry is NOT retired by that: it is about a DIFFERENT and intermittent trigger, and ten clean starts of an intermittent fault is an absence. Original record: patched, two slots, empty store: clean on one start and CORRUPT 3/6 on the NEXT start, same configuration. Re-measured on b10631 (26.08.): 24 of 24 clean over four fresh starts — so the trigger moved, it did not go away. 26.08., official unpatched b10631, -np 2 with --no-kv-unified and speculation: 18 of 18 clean over three fresh starts. On b10577 the same shape on the stock build was CORRUPT 6/6. Not evidence that -np 2 is safe — evidence that the trigger is gone from this workload.
defects.mitigation: -np 1 in every profile. The patch removes one of the two failure modes; it does not make two slots safe. -cram keeps an evicted prefix in RAM, which is what makes a single slot affordable. And since 26.08. something WATCHES for it: setup/scripts/probe.py asks the running model one question whose answer is known, every ten minutes via llama-probe.timer, and restarts the unit when the answer is degenerate. That does not prevent the fault — it moves it from `silent` to `loud`, which is the axis this file sorts by, and it bounds how long a consumer talks to a poisoned server.

defects.title: Restoring a saved prefix into a busy server poisons the context
defects.symptom: After the restore the server produces degenerate output until a fresh start. Production incident 25.08.: the restore landed 0.6 s after two requests had started, while the slots were mid-prefill.
defects.measured: SAME CAUSE AS gfx1151-hip-integrated, established 28.08. On a build containing llama.cpp commit 3181ed701 these cells are CLEAN, and setting GGML_SCHED_UMA_RING=1 -- the switch that commit ships, which turns its graph-input ring buffer off -- makes BOTH prefill cells DIRTY again on the same binary, in the same hour. So a restore is not a second mechanism: llama_state_seq_set_data writes are another concurrent writer into the shared graph-input buffer an integrated device reads while the host writes it. That is also why a restore poisons during another slot's PROMPT PROCESSING and not into an idle server. Measured as a PAIR on 28.08. 08:46 and 08:50, four minutes apart, both sides recording their own environment: with GGML_SCHED_UMA_RING=1 both prefill cells DIRTY, without it both CLEAN. The first version of this measurement (0603) did not record its environment -- the suite could not yet -- and carries a field saying so. Full evidence: bench/reports/2026-08-28_defect1-hunt/HUNT.md, bench/reports/2026-08-28_0846_* and _0850_*. Five cells isolate the ingredient. idle-* clean, which is what pointed at the prefill path rather than at the restore itself. RE-MEASURED 26.08. on the patched b10631 build, and the picture has MOVED: prefill-spec — the cell that matched the production incident of 25.08. exactly — is now CLEAN, along with idle-spec, busy-spec and idle-nospec. The trigger has shifted, the way it shifted for the corruption defect. RE-MEASURED AGAIN 27.08. and the picture is now COMPLETE for the first time: all six cells on b10631, including prefill-nospec, which three earlier runs never reached because the suite aborted at busy-nospec. Six of six CLEAN. The same six on b10631 + llama.cpp PR #27311: six of six CLEAN. That does NOT say the PR changes nothing: both builds carry hip-integrated-off.patch, which is what suppresses the symptom, so the PR was tested on top of its own competitor and there was no corruption in either build for it to fix. The 25.08. run whose prefill cells were DIRTY was the STOCK build (BINARY was hard-wired to build-rocm until commit fcaf6bb on 26.08.), so DIRTY-then and CLEAN-now differ by the patch AND 52 upstream builds. ANSWERED 27.08. late, with a control: the corruption is in upstream master at 5d5cb4c and does NOT reproduce with llama.cpp PR #27311 applied. Eight runs, interleaved. Without the PR and without our patch, the two prefill cells are DIRTY 6 of 6 (stock 54ee5ee once, master 5d5cb4c twice); with the PR on the same tree, CLEAN 6 of 6 over three runs. One variable between those two builds: the PR's 18 commits, rebased onto the same master, marker verified absent in both. Caveat that belongs with it: six clean cells against an intermittent fault is an absence, not an observation, and the dirty side is the stronger half — it reproduced immediately every time. Says nothing about the OTHER gfx1151 defect: hip-integrated-off.patch exists for the plain two-slot corruption with an empty store and no restore, and every cell here involves a restore. Synthesis: bench/reports/2026-08-27_2143_restore-safety-rocm-patched_b10631-18-gc1dcd9825/COMPARISON.md. POSITIVE CONTROL 27.08. 22:33, and it FIRES: the stock build already on disk (build 200, commit 54ee5ee, no patch) reproduces the 25.08. matrix exactly — idle and busy CLEAN, both prefill cells DIRTY, with the probes returning fragments of other contexts instead of 391. So the suite can still see the corruption, and the patched build's clean sheet is a real result rather than an instrument that has gone blind. busy-nospec is CLEAN there at a restore of 278.8 s — under the same 300 s bound the patched build ran past, because the generation simply finished sooner. That is the bound explanation confirmed a second time, by a run not designed to test it. STILL unmeasured: current master without the patch, and current master plus #27311 without the patch, which is the pair that would answer the upstream question. Report: bench/reports/2026-08-27_2233_restore-safety-rocm_b200-54ee5ee. Reports: bench/reports/2026-08-27_2132_restore-safety-rocm-patched_b10631 and 2026-08-27_2143_restore-safety-rocm-patched_b10631-18-gc1dcd9825. What was filed as a hang in its place is withdrawn; see slot-restore-hangs-busy.
defects.mitigation: -np 1, and the gateway restores only into a free slot. Re-run the suite after every llama.cpp build. And since 26.08. something WATCHES for it: setup/scripts/probe.py asks the running model one question whose answer is known, every ten minutes via llama-probe.timer, and restarts the unit when the answer is degenerate. That does not prevent the fault — it moves it from `silent` to `loud`, which is the axis this file sorts by, and it bounds how long a consumer talks to a poisoned server.
defects.status: open — a candidate fix is measured but unmerged upstream

defects.title: GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN costs 41 % prefill on gfx1151
defects.symptom: Nothing is wrong. Prefill is simply 41 % slower, which on a coding agent is the number that decides whether the machine is usable.
defects.measured: 41 % prefill regression, measured elsewhere on gfx1151 and not re-measured here. Checked 26.08.: confirmed gone — build-llama.sh already said so, and the probe now backs the sentence with a source read rather than asking anyone to trust it. `git log -S` places its removal in fa72aeccb (#26046); it had lived in ggml/CMakeLists.txt, ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt and ggml-cuda/vendors/hip.h. The first version of this probe pointed at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt, where it had never been — it would have reported RETIRE? from the first run, which is right by accident and is exactly the crying-wolf failure this registry must not have.
defects.mitigation: Do not pass -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON. setup/scripts/build-llama.sh does not.

upstream_check.while_present: the option still exists upstream — keep leaving it off
upstream_check.when_gone: gone, as build-llama.sh already recorded: removed upstream in fa72aeccb 'HIP: remove rocWMMA FlashAttention' (#26046). The probe's job here is not to discover that but to keep saying it after the note is forgotten

defects.title: The GPU drops the device and takes the process with it
defects.symptom: vk::DeviceLostError, the process dies. The GPU itself recovers completely. Three times in one day, once after about 25 minutes of load.
defects.mitigation: Every service runs under systemd with Restart=on-failure. This is why the stack is not started by hand.

defects.title: Raising the GTT cap removed the ceiling that turned an over-large model into a clean failure
defects.symptom: Below the cap, a model that does not fit fails to allocate and the server exits. Above it, the allocation succeeds against system RAM and the MACHINE goes down instead. It did, on 26.08., during a benchmark.
defects.measured: GTT was raised from 96 to 116 GiB on 26.08. so that a 103.7 GiB quant fits. The same change is what made an over-large one fatal. Seen again 26.08. while measuring Flash-Next: the machine went to about 132 of 134 GB and swap grew to 3.4 GiB. It was not fatal, because only 87.4 GiB of that is pinned GTT and the remaining ~25.6 GiB is the mmap'd PLE table as reclaimable page cache. The gap it exposed is in the guard, not in the arithmetic: bench/run.py refuses a server that does not fit, but only for servers started THROUGH it — the ad-hoc scripts used for those cells started llama-server directly and bypassed it entirely. IT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME the same evening, 26.08. ~22:35, and the journal of the dead boot names it: user.slice peaked at 114.8 GiB with 7.9 of 8 GiB of swap consumed. The desktop stopped responding and the machine had to be power-cycled; every process died with it. Cause: a throwaway script started a second 87 GiB model with `kill; sleep 5` between cells instead of waiting for GTT to fall, so the new allocation landed on one still being torn down. Note the aggravating factor on this box: part of swap is zram, which lives in RAM — under this kind of pressure it cannot free anything, it compresses in place beside 87 GiB of pinned GTT. That is why it froze rather than killing one process. RESOLVED the same night by undoing the cause: the cap went back to 108 GiB. The raise to 116 had been made for a Flash-Next footprint the plan computed as 110 GiB; measured it is 87.4, so the extra 8 GiB bought room nobody needed and cost the ceiling. At 108 the largest model here keeps 20 GiB of headroom and a SECOND one cannot allocate at all — which is the state both of that day's incidents required. A THIRD TIME at 23:11, with the cap already back at 108 and the cgroup limits in place — and it exposed two things the first two had hidden. (a) The limits did not apply: a server started from a script inherits the CALLER's cgroup, and the kernel named it — task_memcg=/user.slice/.../app-com.anthropic.Claude-13190.scope. MemoryMax on llama-user@.service guarded the service and nothing else; what stopped it was a global OOM. (b) The estimate was overridden wrongly by me: BENCH_MODEL_GIB=88 is the GTT footprint, and it silently lowered the HOST check from the file's 103.7 GiB as well — but the 26 GiB that never enters GTT does not evaporate, it is page cache for the mmap and it is resident. The machine survived this one; the OOM killer took the orchestrator, whose `finally` therefore never ran, and production stayed down until a human noticed.
defects.mitigation: Since the third incident: the guard checks TWO numbers against TWO limits — a measured override may correct the GTT estimate and can no longer lower the host-RAM one below the file size; sideserver.py starts the model as a TRANSIENT SYSTEMD UNIT with its own cgroup and its own MemoryMax, because a child process inherits the caller's; and it arms a dead man's switch before stopping anything, so production comes back on a systemd timer even if the orchestrator is killed. Three ceilings, not one, because the first two can still be bypassed: (1) the GTT cap at 108 GiB, so an over-large start fails to allocate instead of hanging the box; (2) MemoryHigh=96G / MemoryMax=108G on llama-user@.service, so the MODEL SERVER is the victim rather than the desktop — verified applicable here, the memory controller is delegated and the model's memory is charged to the unit; (3) zram cut from 8 to 4 GiB, because swap that lives in RAM cannot win against pinned GTT and only delays the failure. bench/sideserver.py is now the ONE way to run a model beside production: it stops the unit, WAITS for GTT to fall, calls check_room_for() which refuses rather than swaps, and tears down in a finally that waits for GTT again before restarting the unit. The guard in bench/run.py was never missing — it was skippable, and twice in one day something skipped it. bench/ refuses to start a server whose weights do not fit, and estimates from the file sizes rather than trusting the caller.

defects.title: Speculative decoding makes a run unrepeatable
defects.symptom: The same question at temperature 0 gives different answers across repetitions. Not wrong answers — different ones, which is worse for a measurement than a wrong one, because it looks like a finding.
defects.measured: bench/suites/spec-determinism.py, 26.08. The divergence bites at near-ties, not at length.
defects.mitigation: Measure correctness with speculation OFF and speed with it ON. bench/ records which was used in every report.

defects.title: -fit cannot model qwen4exp and dies while estimating
defects.symptom: GGML_ASSERT(obj_new) in ggml.c, inside common_params_fit_impl, before the server ever starts. The memory breakdown prints 'unaccounted -47656 MiB' first, which is the estimator failing to model the architecture.
defects.measured: Reported on PR #27742 (26.08., RTX 3090, UD-IQ1_S). Generic fit machinery, not a CUDA path — other hardware is no protection. Not reproduced here yet: nothing can load the model. CONFIRMED by two more reports on 26.08. (RTX 5090, RTX 3090), same GGML_ASSERT(obj_new), and -fit off fixes it for both. Cause identified in-thread by ServeurpersoCom: LLM_ARCH_QWEN4EXP is missing from the graph_max_nodes list in llama-context.cpp, so the fit probe overflows when it tries the MoE-to-system-memory path. Note the shape of it: a 96 GB card never crashes because the model FITS and the probe is never run — which is why our quant is exactly the case that would trigger it: 87.4 GiB measured against a 108 GiB cap leaves the fit probe a reason to try the offload path. FIXED UPSTREAM 27.08. at c52ed2a0b — @ServeurpersoCom's graph_max_nodes diagnosis; reverting that one line brings the assert back at -np 2. MERGED 27.08.2026 as ONE SQUASH COMMIT, 6c84c7d5d — so c52ed2a0b is not a sha in master and cannot be looked for as one; the squash is what carries it. IN THE BINARY WE RUN since the pin moved on 28.08.: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6c84c7d5d build-rocm-patched-b10665-3-gc93d460b6` passes, and the fix is readable in the line the diagnosis named — LLM_ARCH_QWEN4EXP now stands in the graph_max_nodes list at llama-context.cpp:2312. NOT VERIFIED BY A RUN HERE, which is the half that is left: `-fit on` has never been started on this machine with this model. MEASURED HERE 28.08. in the evening, and it does not reproduce: `-fit on` appended to the profile, the pinned build, the estimator RAN (trace: `fitting params to device memory ...`, `getting device memory data for initial parameters`) and fitted -- `projected to use 82525 MiB vs 110337 MiB of free device memory`, `no changes needed`, `successfully fit params` in 0.54 s -- then the server came up and answered. TWO THINGS THE TRACE CORRECTS. The negative `unaccounted` that the bug report quoted just before the assert is NOT the symptom: the probe runs before anything is allocated, so the row balances (110337 + 82525 - 82271 = 110591) and ours prints the same shape while fitting cleanly. And the estimator does not know about demand paging -- it projects 28110 MiB on the host for a table this build keeps at RssAnon 0.31 GiB, so it reasons about a cost we do not pay; here that leaves 27.8 GiB of headroom, in a tighter case it would be the wrong number. Precedence checked in the source, not assumed: the -fit handler (common/arg.cpp:2890) is a plain setter called per occurrence, so the appended `on` beats the profile's `off`, and common_fit_params() is called unconditionally when the flag is set (common/common.cpp:1295). Report: bench/reports/2026-08-28_qwen4exp-merged-verify/REPORT.md. -fit off stays in the profile because it costs nothing there, not because it is still needed.
defects.mitigation: -fit off. It defaults to ON (common/common.h, fit_params = true) and has nothing to do here anyway: every memory parameter in these profiles is set by hand.
defects.status: fixed upstream, verified here 28.08. — the mitigation stays for its own reason

defects.title: Quantised KV crashes on qwen4exp
defects.symptom: GGML_ASSERT(inp->self_k_rot == nullptr && inp->self_v_rot == nullptr) at qwen4exp.cpp:544, for both q8_0 and q4_0.
defects.measured: Reported on PR #27742 (26.08.). Workaround offered there: LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1, or f16. Root cause established in-thread 26.08.: a quantised KV cache is stored Hadamard-rotated to spread outliers before block quantisation, and qwen4exp's graph does not apply or undo that rotation. A fix exists as a separate commit (ServeurpersoCom, 7044fe16) and is NOT in the PR head. f16 remains the answer here either way. FIXED UPSTREAM 27.08. at 0ac4b1802 — q8_0 KV now matches f16: PPL 2.7673 against 2.7507 on UD-IQ1_S. MERGED 27.08.2026 as the squash 6c84c7d5d, so 0ac4b1802 is not a sha in master either, and the pinned build contains the squash (ancestry checked 28.08.). Nothing in the source settles THIS one the way graph_max_nodes settles the fit crash: the rotation inputs are wired generically in llama-graph.cpp and reading them proves nothing about qwen4exp's own graph. MEASURED HERE 28.08. in the evening: `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` on the pinned build, server up, request answered, HTTP 200. The assert fired at GRAPH BUILD, so one request settles it. f16 stays anyway — it was chosen here for output quality, not for this defect: the one q8_0-KV cell measured on 24.08. dropped a long-context task that f16 solved. Report: bench/reports/2026-08-28_qwen4exp-merged-verify/REPORT.md.
defects.mitigation: f16 KV — which was already the choice here for a quality reason: the one q8_0-KV cell measured on 24.08. dropped a long-context task that f16 solved.
defects.status: fixed upstream, verified here 28.08. — the mitigation stays for its own reason

defects.title: Slot save/restore probably does not carry the QSA indexer state
defects.symptom: Unknown in detail, and that is the point. A restored KV cache with an indexer that disagrees with it degrades the output rather than failing.
defects.measured: Not measured — flagged by two reviewers on PR #27742 (26.08.). ggerganov: 'missing state save/load for the indexer'. ngxson: 'otherwise a context save/load will corrupt it'. 28.08., after the merge: THE GAP THEY NAMED IS CLOSED in what landed — llama_memory_hybrid_idx declares state_write/state_read (src/llama-memory-hybrid-idx.h:69-70), and #27755 now runs test-save-load-state across all architectures rather than one. What took its place is a different report on the merged PR (28.08., lviobio): the restore is ACCEPTED and then not used — the next request re-prefills the whole prompt. So the failure reported now is slow where the reviewers feared silent, and neither shape has been measured here. The entry stays open on the silent one: an unmeasured indexer is not made safe by a report about a different symptom.
defects.mitigation: setup/env/flashnext.env carries no --slot-save-path, and AUTO_SAVE=0 belongs in the gateway config while it serves. setup/env/flashnext.env section 4b is the experiment, with idle-nospec as the floor.
defects.status: open — the corruption the reviewers named is addressed in what merged, a reuse failure is reported in its place, neither measured here

defects.title: WITHDRAWN 27.08.2026 — this was our own client timeout, not a hang
defects.symptom: WHAT WAS OBSERVED: POST /slots/0?action=restore did not return while two generations were running. WHAT IT WAS: a restore QUEUES BEHIND THE SLOT IT TARGETS, and bench/suites/restore-safety.py gave it 300 s while filling that slot with a 2,500-token generation that takes 325-341 s without speculation. The bound was shorter than the work, and nothing compared the two. There is no llama.cpp, ROCm or gfx1151 behaviour here.
defects.measured: Reproduced four times (26.08. twice, 27.08. twice, patched b10631 and again on b10631+PR#27311) and withdrawn on the fourth, because the fourth run recorded HOW LONG the restore waited and what it waited for. b10631: idle 0.0 s, prefill-spec 6.2 s against a 77.1 s prefill, prefill-nospec 16.3 s against 78.1 s, busy-spec 68.8 s against a 73.7 s generation — the restore returns when its slot frees. busy-nospec: the generation takes 335.5 s at 7.45 t/s and the bound was 300 s. The asymmetry this entry used to record as unexplained — busy-SPEC clean both times — is the DRAFTER: speculation runs the same counting generation at 33.9 t/s, 4.5x faster, so the wait fits inside the bound. CONFIRMED 27.08. 21:59 with --restore-timeout 900, same build, same cell: generations 325.8 s, restore RETURNED after 319.8 s, probes 391/391/391, generation tails intact. Report: bench/reports/2026-08-27_2159_restore-safety-rocm-patched_b10631.
defects.mitigation: None needed — there is nothing to mitigate. The entry is kept rather than deleted because it was the stated reason -np 2 stayed closed through three sessions: rule (b) of the decision in bench/suites/stock-vs-patched.py requires restore-safety clean in EVERY cell, and the cell was failing against a bound, not against the build. A withdrawn entry that is removed takes its correction with it.
defects.status: withdrawn — not a defect, the measurement bound was shorter than the workload

defects.title: The QSA indexer cache desyncs from the attention cache across slots
defects.symptom: GGML_ASSERT(mctx_idx->get_n_kv() == inp->mctx->get_attn()->get_n_kv() && "the indexer cache must track the attention cache cell for cell") at qwen4exp.cpp:285, during prompt processing, the first time a request lands on a DIFFERENT slot than the previous one.
defects.measured: Reported 26.08. on PR #27742 (Windows, RTX 5090, UD-Q4_K_XL, this branch at 035e227). Not reproduced here. The detail that matters: it was hit WITHOUT passing --parallel, because llama-server defaults to n_slots = 4 — so anyone who simply does not set -np gets four slots and this defect. FIXED UPSTREAM 27.08. at cfbdc0a50 — and the cause was NOT the scheduler but the SERVER PROMPT CACHE: on the old build --cache-ram 0 completes where the default asserts on the third request. MERGED 27.08.2026 as the squash 6c84c7d5d, and the pinned build contains it (ancestry checked 28.08.). The SOURCE DOES NOT CONFIRM IT and is not expected to: the assert still stands, at qwen4exp.cpp:309 in master — the announced cause was the server prompt cache, not the assert, so a grep for the assert would say 'still broken' about a fix that works. MEASURED HERE 28.08. in the evening, and the first attempt PROVED NOTHING — worth keeping, because it looked like a pass: three SEQUENTIAL requests at -np 2 all returned 200 and /slots shows all three landed on slot 1 while slot 0 stayed empty. The defect needs a request on a DIFFERENT slot than the previous one, so sequential traffic cannot provoke it. Concurrent traffic can: at -np 2 two requests ran overlapping on slots 1 and 0 and a third then took slot 0 by LCP similarity; at -np 4 -- the shape it was REPORTED in, since llama-server defaults to four slots -- four requests ran on four distinct slots and a fifth followed on slot 0. No assert, health=200, answers coherent. The server prompt cache, which is the announced cause rather than the scheduler, was active throughout: the profile carries -cram 4096. -np 1 stays regardless, for the two reasons above it, which are properties of this GPU and untouched by anything upstream merged. Report: bench/reports/2026-08-28_qwen4exp-merged-verify/REPORT.md.
defects.mitigation: -np 1, explicitly. This is the third independent reason for it on this stack, after the gfx1151 HIP race and the restore hang — and the first that is a property of the ARCHITECTURE rather than of the GPU, so it would apply on any hardware.

defects.title: The PLE table is loaded into RAM because `auto` turns mmap off on an iGPU
defects.symptom: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next holds its 26.82 GiB per_layer_token_embd table in ANONYMOUS memory instead of reading it from the mapping on demand, so the model needs ~27 GiB more resident than it should and does not fit on this machine. Nothing says so: there is no error, no warning, and the only positive signal is a log line the server does not print unless -v is passed. The cost lands as swap pressure and, without a memory guard, as a hung machine.
defects.measured: 28.08.2026, three runs, same model and profile, `-c 8192 -cram 0`, probe read straight after /slots. master b10665-1 with the default `auto`: load_mode resolves to none, no lazy read, RssAnon 27.13 GiB, peak RSS 28.06, run ended with the machine at 7.1 GiB available and 140 MiB of swap. Same build with `--load-mode mmap`: lazy read DOES engage, but the whole model then loads through the mapping -- buffers stood after 33 s instead of 4 and the server had not answered /slots after 7 minutes. master + PR #27837, default load mode: `load_mode = none` (weights keep the fast path) AND `lazy read enabled` for the 27465 MiB tensor, RssAnon 0.31 GiB, peak RSS 1.27, up in 19 s. 27.13 -> 0.31 is the whole defect. CAUSE, read in the source rather than guessed: ggml-cuda.cu:4845 sets `mmap_support = props->type != IGPU`, the type comes from `prop.integrated` at :4819, and the 8060S is integrated; one device without mmap turns it off for the WHOLE model (llama-model.cpp:1402), and TENSOR_READ_LAZY requires use_mmap (llama-model-loader.cpp:1290). Note this is NOT reached by our hip-integrated-off.patch: that sets info.devices[id].integrated, a different copy of the flag. PR STATE, checked 28.08. in the evening: #27837 is unchanged in content since the cherry-pick (head 280e76452, which is the commit this build carries), but MASTER MOVED UNDER IT — #27881 (50f068fff) renamed LLAMA_TENSOR_READ_LAZY_* to LLAMA_LAZY_MODE_* and the PR no longer applies cleanly. A rebuild on a newer master therefore has to adapt the cherry-pick, and then MEASURE AGAIN rather than carry the 26.82 GiB over: the figure belongs to a build, which is the rule budget.lazy_relief() enforces anyway.
defects.mitigation: Build with PR #27837 cherry-picked on top of master and the gfx1151 patch; setup/env/flashnext.env pins that build in LLAMA_BIN and explains why. #27837 maps the lazy tensor ALONE and leaves the weights on the fast path -- `--load-mode mmap` is not a substitute, it mmaps everything and the load does not finish in a usable time. setup/lib/budget.py grants the MODEL_LAZY_GIB relief only when the binary about to run IS that pinned build, so reverting LLAMA_BIN withdraws the relief and the guard refuses the profile rather than letting it overrun.

detect.how: Start the server with `-v --log-file X` and grep X for `lazy read enabled`. Present, together with `load_mode = none`, means the fix is in and the table is demand-paged. Absent means the table is being copied into RAM. RssAnon on the llama-server process settles the same question after the fact: ~27 GiB exposed, ~0.3 GiB guarded.

upstream_check.while_present: #27837 has landed in master -- the lazy read no longer depends on the load mode. Rebuild from master, re-measure RssAnon on Flash-Next, and if it is ~0.3 GiB the cherry-pick can go and LLAMA_BIN can follow the normal build again.
upstream_check.when_gone: master still gates TENSOR_READ_LAZY on use_mmap, so on this iGPU the PLE table is loaded in full. Keep the #27837 cherry-pick, and keep LLAMA_BIN pinned to the build that carries it.
upstream_check.note: The pattern names the FIX, not the cause, so present_means is retire -- the same shape as gfx1151-hip-integrated after 28.08. It reads the source and not the pull request's state on purpose: #27794 merged and did nothing for this machine, so 'merged' is not the signal. What changed the measurement is one condition in one file, and that is what is watched. And it survived the rename that broke the pull request on 28.08.: the pattern sits in init_mappings and is about mmap, not about the enum #27881 renamed. Master's gate still reads `(flags & TENSOR_READ_LAZY) && use_mmap && lazy_mode != LLAMA_LAZY_MODE_OFF`, so nothing moved for this machine.

defects.title: The automatic prefix save throws the current prefix out of the slot
defects.symptom: A request the gateway reports as `warm` takes cold time. Nothing errors and nothing in the log disagrees with itself: the gateway's warm/cold verdict means 'I have seen this prefix', not 'llama.cpp still holds it', and only the second question is what the clock measures. Seen as a 19x slowdown on a prefix that was warm seconds earlier.
defects.measured: 28.08.2026, qwen38, a 24-tool synthetic prefix, AUTO_SAVE off so the saves were the only ones. A warm: 0.7 s / 4 tokens evaluated. Save of a DIFFERENT prefix B: 12.7 s. A again: 13.6 s / 1950 tokens -- 19x, and 1950 tokens the server already had. Save of the SAME prefix A: 12.8 s. A again: 1.5 s, unaffected. CAUSE: saving a prefix means putting it INTO the slot, and with -np 1 there is one slot. The save straight after a cold request is harmless because the slot already holds that prefix -- which is why the first attempt to measure this concluded the save was innocent: it tested only the same-prefix case. What bites is that auto_save is asynchronous (asyncio.create_task in cc-gateway.py) and slow: 101.9 s measured for one automatic save on this machine. So the user moves on to prefix B while the save of A is still running, the save then puts A back into the slot, and B -- correctly reported warm -- is prefilled from scratch.
defects.mitigation: None in place. AUTO_SAVE=0 in ~/.config/cc-gateway.env removes it and gives up disk restore with it, which on this machine is the difference between a 0.7 s and an 85 s cold start -- so it is a trade, not a fix. A real fix would have the save not disturb the serving slot: run it while the slot is idle, or put the evicted prefix back after saving, or give the save its own slot (-np 2, which this hardware has its own defect against -- see gfx1151-two-slots).

detect.how: bench/suites/save-eviction.py. It measures both cases -- saving a different prefix and saving the same one -- because only the pair distinguishes this defect from a save that is merely slow.
